exposure: Mode of birth (C-section vs. spontaneous delivery)
cohort: The study included 207 newly admitted risk newborns, comprising both preterm and term infants.
finding: TREC levels calculated for the 5th percentile in a risk neonatal group are suggested as a surrogate marker for an increased risk of fatal septic complications.
mod_finding: Neonates born by C-section were found to have higher TREC levels compared to neonates born by spontaneous delivery.
cross-section timing: Dry blood spot samples were collected during the years 2015-2018 from newly admitted risk newborns.
gest_age: Preterm and term newborns were included in the study.
